curation.notes: STAR Protocols methods paper describing how to measure whole-cell mechanical properties with a LUMICKS C-Trap: 3.15 µm polystyrene beads are optically trapped and pushed into adherent cells (one trap) or suspended cells (two traps, one indenting and one stabilizing) under constant-force feedback (50-100 pN, up to 31.3 Hz feedback) to obtain force-deformation curves. Cell-scale indentation rather than single-molecule manipulation; no specific cell line or results given.

evidence.snippet: Aim for a trap stiffness around 0.20–0.25 pN/nm.

filter_frequency.note: maximum force-feedback update frequency of the C-Trap, not a filter

evidence.snippet: It is advised to use the maximum possible feedback frequency. For the LUMICKS C-Trap, the maximum frequency is 31.3 Hz.
Prepare the bead solution by diluting the stock solution polystyrene beads (5% w/v, 3.15 μm average diameter) 1:200 in sterile PBS.

entities.name: Living cells (adherent or suspended; cell type not specified)

evidence.snippet: we present a protocol to quantify these properties on living cells by applying piconewton-range forces with optically trapped microspheres

solution.buffer: DMEM GlutaMAX + 10% FBS + 1% penicillin-streptomycin, supplemented with HEPES (live cell medium)
